big: Three brothers inherited a shop from their father. For years they argued over who owned what share. A short written agreement, signed by all, would have ended the quarrel on day one.

lines: I keep hearing about HUF, trusts and gift deeds. Which one is for me?
They are different tools for different needs. Learn what each does, and then ask a lawyer and a tax adviser which fits your family. Education only, not advice.

rows: A Hindu undivided family, a separate entity for tax
Trustees hold assets for named beneficiaries, as per the deed
A document that transfers an asset without payment
An agreement among family members on sharing property
note: A gift of property usually needs a registered deed. Tax and stamp duty rules apply, so check first.

title: Family structures
stops: An HUF is a separate entity for tax
A family trust is a kind of bank account
A gift deed transfers an asset without payment
A family settlement makes disputes more likely
caps: It applies to Hindu, Buddhist, Jain and Sikh families.
In a trust, trustees hold assets for named beneficiaries under a deed.
A parent can gift a flat to a child by a registered deed.
A written settlement is meant to prevent disputes.

q: Parents want assets held by trustees for their child, as set out in a deed. Which tool is this?
why: A gift deed transfers an asset to another person without payment.
A codicil changes or adds to an existing will.
A succession certificate confirms who may claim a dead person's assets.
In a family trust, trustees hold assets for named beneficiaries.

q: Rohan wants to give his flat to his daughter during his life. Which document is used?
opts: A shop receipt for the flat
A bank brochure on the flat
A verbal promise made to her
why: A shop receipt cannot transfer a flat to anyone.
A gift deed transfers an asset, and property needs registration.
A brochure describes products and cannot transfer ownership.
A verbal promise does not transfer ownership of a flat.

q: Siblings sign a written agreement on how to share an ancestral property. What is this?
why: An HUF return is a tax filing and not an agreement among siblings.
A premium notice is from an insurer and has no link to property.
A family settlement is an agreement that settles how property is shared.
A stop-loss is an order type in share trading.

q: Dadi hears that an HUF helps with tax. What should she do first?
opts: Ask a lawyer and a tax adviser
Form one at once, since friends did
Ignore it, as tax never changes
Tell the bank to make one for her
why: Rules depend on the family and facts, so ask experts first.
A friend's choice may not suit her family, so copying is risky.
Tax rules do change, so ignoring them is not a plan.
A bank does not form an HUF for any customer.

pts: A family trust: trustees hold assets for named beneficiaries.
A gift deed transfers an asset. Property gifts usually need registration.
A written family settlement can prevent disputes.
